## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [14. Mai 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.132
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.132
- Datum: 14.5.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Wyndham Hotel
42 West 58th Street
New York

24. 5. 41

Dear Hanna & Manfred,
We just received your letter of May 13th and
hasten to reply before we begin the daily work. I am very glad
that by fulfilling your engament[?] and visiting Harrogate you
missed one of the heaviest attacks on London, but I pity you,
Hanna, that the torture at the dentist's was prolonged for another
week. At this moment, however, I hope that you are already en-
joying the quieter atmosphere of Bath, having no more dentist to
be afraid of, and all the advantages which the garden can offer.
Now first the replies to some of your questions,
Eva. I shall make more detailed enquiries about the school and
the prospects when returning to England to continue school or
university. For that purpose I shall enquire at the Childs
study Association where I met a lady who has lived in England
for some time, had a school of her own in Hamstead and has
children who go to school here. As her job at the committee is to
advise parents and guardian about education she can certainly
help me. I will also write to Miss Baker from whom Eva and
I had very nice letters and who, being in one of the most
expensive and exclusive colleges, will be in a position to
give reliable information. - About the two schools in Croton:
the private (progressive, that is very modern) school and the public
school where Eva goes now, I had made enquiries before
deciding to settle Eva at Mrs. Sch.'s. The information I got
from Mrs. Sch. and other people was that both schools are good.
The reason why I first decided for the private school was -
in spite of its ultra-modern education and teaching methods-
that most of the children of Amity Hall go there while only
3 or 4 go to the public school with Eva. The private school has
been for a long time very generous with scholarships and
Mrs. Sch. prefers it, as far as I can make out mainly for
the reason that the "art" classes are so very good and
because she is personally on very good terms with all of them
while with the public school which is a school about the
size of the Bath school, also a very new and modern building,
is of course more impersonal. Where she learns more in the
old-fashioned sense of the word, is difficult to decide.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier. Die Tinte ist blau-violett. Die Lesbarkeit ist gut.

pages.transcription:
2)
The private school which has only a hundred pupils in
all and where the children are taught in groups of 6 or 8
is of course much more individual and it may be that in some
cases a much more rapid progress is possible. On the other hand
it is doubtful whether their method of giving the children as
much freedom as possible in their work and make them do things
by trying to get them interested in it and never force them to do a
thing in the given moment, will always work. - I discussed
all those problems with everybody I could get hold of at that time
and I am still at the same point that both systems have their
definite advantages and disadvantages. - Both schools lead up to
the college which is something between high school and uni-
versity, and I do not think that except in a few very snobbish
schools public school education would be a disadvantage.
As to languages I wrote you a few weeks ago. In her present
school Eva will get French and Latin next February, and she
has a good chance at Amity Hall where they will have a French
councellor - that is a person who is something between a teacher,
playmate and matron - and where her friend Marion speaks it
fluently. - That they should think her "inferior" in her school
I cannot believe; this must be the personal opinion of one
child and she certainly does not take it seriously, for she neither
mentioned it to me or to Mrs. Sch. and from what she tells me I
had always the impression that she likes going there. There is
one teacher whom she does not like - but that will happen in every
school. - One thing may be a little hard for her and the
other public school children at Amity Hall, and that is that
the private school closes already next week whereas the public
school continues another month. But as the school finishes
at 3 anyway she still has the whole afternoon with the others.
About your brothers affidavit we made an
enquiry last week through Washington's Visa Department and
they may let us know in due time how his matter stands.
But they are slow and it may also take weeks before we get a
reply although we asked them to make telegraphic enquiries.
I am glad that Bath and Rosemount are as
pleasant for you as ever and I do long for the moment
when we will all be there again, together. But when will
that be?
Love and kisses, keep well and
take good care of yourself,
Lotte.
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes, handschriftlich. Die Tinte ist blau-violett.
Dies ist eine Kopie von Seite 3 mit aufgelegten Archivierungshilfen (Farb- und Grauskala).

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift ist klar. Ein Wort ('engament') ist eine offensichtliche Verschreibung der Autorin für 'engagement'.
